The Senior Director of Student & Academic Affairs is responsible for strategic and operational management of all student services for the School of Journalism. The position provides assistance to the Dean, the Associate Dean, the faculty, and students in academic advising, recruitment, admissions, financial aid, the evaluation and awarding of fellowships and block grant funds, student orientation and events, career counseling, and related programs and supervises four full-time career staff working in these areas. The position reports to the Chief Administrative Officer and receives broad directives on initiatives, working independently and strategically to create and sustain a welcoming and inclusive student culture and climate.

Directs a team of four professional student services staff who provide the full range of academic advising to department students and service to Department Chairs/Deans, Faculty, and prospective students.
Monitors and evaluates employee performance, salary actions, hiring decisions, and other human resources-related issues of managed staff.
Recommends employee selection and corrective action to the Chief Administrative Officer.
Responsible for ensuring appropriate and ongoing training of student services staff, as needed.
Leads the student services staff in the planning and implementation of high-visibility events, e.g., orientation, Journalism showcases, and commencement.
Provides direction to student services advisers on complex student matters.

Manages and supervises the Admissions Director and the Director of Career Services staff in developing strategic initiatives, administering the budget, assessing the needs of the student services unit, and innovating new approaches to achieve the unit's goals.
Recognizes issues with campus impact or future implications and advises managed employees accordingly.
Program Strategy Development
Develops, interprets, and administers student services programs. Full functional responsibility and authority for planning, directing, and evaluating all aspects of the student services programs.
Leads curriculum planning, classroom scheduling, enrollment management, including Concurrent Enrollment and ASE hiring.
Leads student financial aid and fellowships. Develops funding models for our student groups and advocates on their behalf.
Evaluates the effectiveness of the student academic advising function, and makes changes to the program to provide better service to organizational management, faculty, and students.

Leveraging current systems and utilizing new technology, works to streamline systems and business processes related to major applications, student records, and other student-related activities and services.
Works effectively with people from diverse cultures on issues such as performance management, organizational change, workplace climate, and related topics.
Works with faculty on initiatives around diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
Coordinates with development staff on various fundraising efforts and supports the School's alumni relationship-building efforts.
Serves on School committees, as needed.
Plans, develops, and administers the school's student services budget of roughly $100,000 and student financial aid budget of roughly $1.6 million.
Monitors the budget's progress and effectiveness, ensuring operations run smoothly and meet objectives.
Submits the annual budget, participates in quarterly budget reviews, and responds to forecasts.
Leads monthly audit on spending.
Provides broad directives to staffing of operational areas within the unit.
Decides which resources will be committed to goals and objectives and how they will be allocated.
Evaluates school resources dedicated to operations and decides management for equipment care, building maintenance and access, staffing and resources of key events, and advises employees accordingly.
Student Advising & Hiring

Applying advanced academic advising concepts and experience, identifies and refers for resolution intricate student issues, such as alleged discrimination, complex grade disputes, and students' personal crises.
Serves as department agent in interventions for students emotionally or psychologically at risk.
May personally provide students with academic advice on progression and requirements.
Represents the student academic unit to the campus community and relevant external constituencies.
Serves as a resource for information and training of faculty on university policies and procedures surrounding grades, including grade changes, grade appeals, and the removal of Incompletes.
Maintains and secures grade sheets and final course grade reports.
Provides advice to instructors about issues concerning grades, DSP accommodations, suspected academic misconduct, and other procedural/policy matters.
Recognizes issues that have campus-wide impact or future implications and advises managed employees, faculty, Managers, Vice Chairs, and the Chair accordingly.
Leads the recruitment, assignment, and onboarding of approximately 10 ASEs each year: tutors, readers, and GSIs.
Participates in ongoing professional development.

Embraces the strategic goal of creating an equitable and inclusive program that fully honors the diversity of our students, faculty, and staff and expands opportunities for those from underserved backgrounds and communities.
Knowledge of common university-specific computer application programs
Advanced knowledge of university and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences in a higher education environment.
Knowledge of departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences in a higher education environment.
Skills in monitoring/assessing people, processes, or services to make improvements.
Skills in project management, social perceptiveness to be aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.
Ability in problem identification and reasoning.
Ability to develop original ideas to solve problems using persuasion and leadership.
